get.description:
One collection with its items in order.

404 -- never 403 -- when the caller's level is insufficient, so the response
does not disclose that a private collection exists.

Two upstream calls, in this order and not the other: the viewer level must be
resolved against *this collection's* creator, and the creator is not known
until we ask. Reading the collection first and retrying would never work --
a `connections` collection 404s on the first call, so the creator id we would
need to earn access to it is exactly what the failed response does not
contain. The same shape as the attachment serve path.

get.description:
Public profile read. Resolves username → profile_id, then forwards with
the viewer's access level. Owners use /profiles/me for the full shape; this
route always returns the public (visibility-filtered) shape.

**`lang` is a passthrough.** The resolution, the published set and the
per-field languages come back from profile-service in `content_language` and
are relayed untouched. There is deliberately no public translations route
beside this one: a reader gets a translated profile by asking for the profile
in a language, and a second read path would drift from the first.

get.description:
The public listing, paged. Takes either `offset` (the numbered-page
control the web listing renders) or `cursor` (load-more / infinite clients);
the response carries both keys either way. See
docs/architecture/pagination.md.

**The same rows for everyone, signed in or not.** No viewer is forwarded, so
an author browsing here -- including their own profile's publications tab,
which is this route under `author_id` -- sees the public listing exactly as a
stranger does. Their `private` and `by_link` work lives on
`/publications/me`.

get.description:
Find the caller's own publication carrying this `import_key`.

The lookup an importer does before deciding create-or-update, and the only
public read that reports the caller's `removed` and draft rows. Those are
exactly the rows whose keys still occupy the unique index, so an importer
that cannot see them creates and takes a 409 that repeats forever (#663).

Owner-scoped, so reporting a soft-deleted row leaks nothing: the caller is
its author. Not merged into `/publications/me` -- one query parameter should
not change which rows an endpoint may reveal.

`relay_response`, not `relay_with_authors`: the shape carries no byline to
enrich.

BackgroundColor.description:
A collection's background: a solid colour or a two-stop gradient.

Gradient values carry a hyphen (`green-blue`), which is not a Python
identifier, so those members are named with an underscore and reachable by
value (`BackgroundColor("green-blue")`). The wire value is the hyphenated
one; nothing needs attribute access, since values arrive off the wire.

`CollectionDetail.items` carries only a first page since 2026-08-15; this is
how a reader reaches the rest of a long reading list. `items_count` on the
detail body is how they know there is more.

ContentLanguage.description:
Relayed verbatim from the domain service.

The contract is `docs/architecture/content-language.md`. The BFF neither
computes nor reshapes any member of it: `served`, `available` and `primary`
are the domain service's answers, and the frontend reads its canonical, its
hreflang set and its redirect decision from them. Recomputing any of it here
would fork the resolver, and the two copies would disagree the first time a
field fell back.
ContentLanguage.title: ContentLanguage

ContributorRole.description:

scripts/check-enum-parity.py. The frontend renders `author` in the run-in
byline and every other value as a credit after it ("Compiled by ...").
ContributorRole.title: ContributorRole

LanguageProficiency.description:
A language the person says they speak, and how well.

**`code` is what makes this data rather than a string.** The field shipped
with `name` only -- free text, so the stored values are "English", "French",
"German", "Russian": no code, nothing to match a search filter against,
nothing to render in another interface language, and no way to tell
"Chinese" from "Mandarin" from a typo. `code` is the fix, and `name` stays
beside it so the rows written before it still render.

**Validated against the whole catalogue, not the authorable set.** This is a
claim about a *person*, not content they authored: a researcher who speaks
Hungarian should be able to say so on a site that does not offer Hungarian
as a writing language. `is_authorable_language` is for the languages someone
may write in; this is not one of those fields.

Optional because the rows already in the database have no code and must keep
loading. A write that omits it is accepted and simply carries less.
LanguageProficiency.title: LanguageProficiency

MarkdownViewState.description:
A file face's converted markdown: on the page, kept off it, or absent.
Mirrors publications-service's `MarkdownViewState`.
MarkdownViewState.title: MarkdownViewState

MentionTarget.description:
One entry of the `mentions` map: the profile a `@handle` in the body names.

`username` is the profile's **current** handle, which is not necessarily the
one the body was written with -- profile-service resolves old handles through
UsernameHistory, so a rename heals every mention of that profile rather than
stranding it. The renderer links and labels the chip from this field.
MentionTarget.title: MentionTarget

OrganizationCard.description:
The organization a publication was published under, resolved from
`affiliated_org_id` by the BFF. The five fields a top bar and a link need
-- deliberately not `OrganizationSummary`, whose member counts and claim
state are the org page's business, not a publication's.
OrganizationCard.title: OrganizationCard

PrimaryFormat.description:
Which view of a file face the work page leads with: the file (default),
or the markdown with the file as its PDF view. Mirrors publications-service's

PrimaryFormat.title: PrimaryFormat

ProfileMe.description: Owner view — every field, every visibility flag.
ProfileMe.title: ProfileMe

ProfilePublic.description: Public view — gated by is_public and per-field toggles.
ProfilePublic.title: ProfilePublic

ProfileStats.description:
Counts and tab-presence for the profile header (#1077).

Aggregated at the BFF per request from four services, never stored. Each
field is None when its leg failed, and the frontend treats None as
"unknown" -- it keeps the tab and drops the number -- never as zero or
empty. `followers_count` and `works_count` are the same for every viewer;
`has_cv` and `has_timetable` are resolved at the caller's real access
level, so they say whether *this* viewer would find anything on the tab.
ProfileStats.title: ProfileStats

PublicationAuthorInvite.description:
One name to put on the byline, as a client asks for it.

Deliberately narrower than publications-service's shape: that one also
carries `account_less`, the assertion that the invitee has no account and
so is credited without an answer (#1003). A client must not be able to say
that -- it would be instant attribution without consent, the impersonation
primitive the pending state exists to prevent. This tier decides it, off
profile-service's `has_account`, and stamps it on the forwarded body
(`stamp_account_less`). Pydantic drops an unknown field a client sends.
PublicationAuthorInvite.title: PublicationAuthorInvite

PublicationAuthorOut.description:
One name on the byline, with the profile card resolved.

`author` is null when profile-service could not be reached -- embedding is
best-effort, and a byline entry with an unresolved card still tells the
reader someone is there.
PublicationAuthorOut.title: PublicationAuthorOut

PublicationImportRef.description:
What an importer needs to decide create-or-update, and nothing else.

Mirrors publications-service's schema of the same name. Deliberately not
`PublicationOut`: this is the one owner-scoped read that reports
soft-deleted rows, and a removed publication is content its author withdrew,
so the response carries the row's identity and state rather than its body.
PublicationImportRef.title: PublicationImportRef

PublicationType.description:
Every type libretimes.io may create -- living content and, since
2026-09-14, the five citable record types.

This was deliberately a subset excluding `original_research`, `letter`,
`review`, `report` and `thesis`, because journal-bff was the door for
them. The journal is parked (ONE-PRODUCT Phase 0) and its return is a
venue over the same rows, so the record types are creatable here with
the semantics publications-service enforces by type alone: frozen on
publish, numbered, retracted not deleted, corrected by a new version
(WORKS-UNIFICATION decision 15). The chooser says so before Publish.

See docs/architecture/content-types.md.
PublicationType.title: PublicationType

PublicationWorkBlock.description:
What the publication page shows of its work row. A subset of `Work`
on purpose: the page already renders the text, byline and categories.
PublicationWorkBlock.title: PublicationWorkBlock

Reference.description:
A bibliographic reference on a publication. CSL-aligned snapshot; may link
to a known work or a library citation. Mirrors publications-service.
Reference.title: Reference

ReorderRequest.description: The full ordered list of entity ids. `position` becomes the index here.
ReorderRequest.title: ReorderRequest

RetractionOut.description:
The withdrawal notice publications-service carries on every read of a
retracted record (its `RetractionOut`). A retracted record stays readable
so citations do not dangle, which is exactly why the notice has to reach
the page: a reader who followed a citation here needs it before the text.
RetractionOut.title: RetractionOut
